title: Dropdown
lead: Dropdown also known as Select, is used to choose an item from a collection of options.

examples.name: Basic
prose: Dropdown is used as a controlled component with value and onChange properties along with an options collection. Label and value of an option are defined with the optionLabel and optionValue properties respectively. Default property name for the optionLabel is label and value for the optionValue. If optionValue is omitted and the object has no value property, the object itself becomes the value of an option. Note that, when options are simple primitive values such as a string array, no optionLabel and optionValue would be necessary.

examples.name: Checkmark
prose: An alternative way to highlight the selected option is displaying a checkmark instead.

examples.name: Editable
prose: When editable is present, the input can also be entered with typing.

examples.name: Group
prose: Options can be grouped when a nested data structures is provided. To define the label of a group optionGroupLabel property is needed and also optionGroupChildren is required to define the property that refers to the children of a group.

examples.name: Template
prose: Options and the selected option display support templating with itemTemplate and valueTemplate properties respectively.

examples.name: Filter
prose: Dropdown provides built-in filtering that is enabled by adding the filter property.

examples.name: Clear Icon
prose: When showClear is enabled, a clear icon is added to reset the Dropdown.

examples.name: Loading State
prose: Loading state can be used loading property.

examples.name: Virtual Scroll
prose: VirtualScroller is used to render a long list of options efficiently like 100K records in this demo. The configuration is done with virtualScrollerOptions property, refer to the VirtualScroller for more information about the available options as it is used internally by Dropdown.

examples.name: Float Label
prose: A floating label appears on top of the input field when focused.

examples.name: Filled
prose: Specify the variant property as filled to display the component with a higher visual emphasis than the default outlined style.

examples.name: Invalid
prose: Invalid state is displayed using the invalid prop to indicate a failed validation. You can use this style when integrating with form validation libraries.

examples.name: Disabled
prose: When disabled is present, the element cannot be edited and focused.
